paragraphs.text: # dsh-web-fetch-moli
中文 · GitHub
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin providing a **Moli** backend for the `web_fetch` tool. Built on Moli
(an ultra-lightweight Rust headless browser), it renders dynamic micro-frontends, single-page appli
cations (SPAs), and static sites in a memory footprint an order of magnitude below a full Chromium/P
laywright stack, denoises pages via **LinkeDOM + Readability + mdream**, and returns clean, LLM-opti
mized GitHub Flavored Markdown.
## Key Highlights
- **Lightweight Footprint** — A local daemon costs single-digit MB at rest and tens of MB while rend
ering (measured below), so high concurrency stays viable on resource-constrained servers. See Measur

ed footprint for the numbers and their conditions.
- **Enterprise Micro-Frontend & Dynamic SPA Compa
tibility** — Bypasses Content Security Policy (`Page.setBypassCSP`), bypasses Service Worker caching
, and can optionally ignore TLS certificate errors (`ignoreCertificateErrors`, off by default). Driv
es native Moli layout tree computation via CDP Micro-Clip layout materialization (`Page.captureScree
nshot` 1x1 micro-viewport) and triggers W3C standard `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` without
any user-script monkey-patching, cleanly rendering complex micro-frontends (Alibaba Alfa, qiankun, s

ingle-spa) that require full dynamic-script execution.
- **Two Flexible Backends**:
- `local` *(defa
ult)*: Automatically manages a local `moli serve` daemon over CDP, providing full SPA and micro-fron

tend execution.
- `cdp`: Connects to an existing remote Moli or Chromium CDP service over Chrome Dev

Tools Protocol.
- **High-Performance Two-Stage Denoise Pipeline** — LinkeDOM + Mozilla Readability e
xtracts primary content and eliminates noise (ads, nav bars, footers, forms), followed by mdream (Ru
st native with pure JS fallback) for high-fidelity, LLM-optimized Markdown conversion. Inline base64

images are elided to compact size placeholders.
- **Cloudflare Challenge Resilience** — Detects `cf
-mitigated: challenge` interstitials and waits in the same page/context for natural clearance withou
t artificial bot behavior.

## Measured footprint
Moli is a single Rust process (no separate browser + driver + renderer tree), so its resident set st

ays far below a
full Chromium stack. The plugin ships **no benchmark harness** — the numbers below a

re one measurement on one machine,
recorded here so the claim is reproducible rather than asserted.
Treat them as an order of magnitude, not a guarantee.
Conditions: Moli `1.1.9`, Linux x86_64, one daemon started with `moli serve`, `VmHWM` (peak resident

set) summed over
all `moli` processes from `/proc/<pid>/status`, 5s settle after each `Page.navigat
e`, single tab, no concurrency.
| State | Peak RSS (`VmHWM`) |

| Daemon started, no page loaded | 13.2 MB |
| After one light static page (`example.com`) | 55.9 MB

|
| After one heavy article page (Wikipedia, long article + assets) | 99.6 MB |
Two things a single headline number would hide: the resting cost is small, but **a heavy page can pu

sh one daemon to
roughly 100 MB**, and the process does not shrink back after the page is closed (th

e high-water mark stays). Budget per
concurrent fetch accordingly rather than multiplying one number
by your concurrency.
Comparison with other engines is deliberately qualitative here: this repository contains no measurem

ents of Chromium,
Lightpanda, or Obscura, and this project has not run their test suites, so no per-

product figures or failure claims are
made. What can be stated from this repository's own code and t

ests: the plugin drives Moli over CDP, bypasses CSP for
dynamic script loading, and materializes lay
out via Micro-Clip screenshots so `IntersectionObserver` sentinels fire.
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness (`dsh web`) ≥ `0.2.1-rc.3`, Node.js ≥ 22 (the plugin drives CDP over the native g

lobal `WebSocket`, which Node 20 does not provide).
- **Zero manual setup**: the plugin features **a
utomatic download on first use**. If no `moli` binary is detected, it downloads and unpacks the late
st release binary matching your OS and architecture (Linux, macOS, Windows x86_64 / arm64) into `~/.

cache/moli`.
- Existing installations are detected in this order: the `moliPath` setting → the `MOLI
_PATH` environment variable → `~/.cache/moli/moli` → `moli` on `$PATH`. There is **no scan of `~/.lo
cal/bin`**; if you install Moli there, either put it on `$PATH` or set `moliPath`.

Manual installation (optional). The release archive unpacks into a versioned directory
(`moli-v1.1.9
-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/`), so `--strip-components=1` is required to land the binary at a predicta
nknown-linux-gnu/`), so `--strip-components=1` is required to land the binary at a predictable path:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That places the binary at `~/.local/bin/moli`, which is **not** a default search location for this p

lugin — export it on
`PATH` (most distributions already include `~/.local/bin` there) or point the `

moliPath` setting at it. On Windows the
asset is a `.zip` whose archive members sit under the same v

ersioned directory; extract it and point `moliPath` at the
resulting `moli.exe`.
## Installation
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> **npm status:** `dsh-web-fetch-moli` is **not yet on the npm registry**
> (`https://registry.npmjs

.org/dsh-web-fetch-moli` returns 404 as of 0.8.0), so the bare-name form will fail today.
> Use the
`github:` form above. `CONTRIBUTING.md` states how an npm release is produced.
After adding, restart `dsh web` to load the plugin.
## Configuration
Every option is a **volatile field of this row's Config**: since DSH 0.1.7 the settings domain serve
s the form from the profile entry itself, so a save applies live — no restart and no plugin remount.
Open *dsh-web-fetch-moli* on the DSH Plugins page to edit it:
| Field | Default | Description |

| `backend` | `local` | `local` (managed Moli CDP daemon) or `cdp` (remote CDP endpoint). |
| `moliP
ath` | *(auto)* | Path to `moli` binary. Blank = discover via `MOLI_PATH`, `~/.cache/moli`, then `$P

ATH`. |
| `cdpEndpoint` | `127.0.0.1:9222` | Remote CDP endpoint (`host:port` or URL, used in `cdp`

mode). |
| `shareBrowserContext` | `true` | Preserves cookies and localStorage across fetches in `cd

p` mode. Unchecked (and always in `local` mode): fresh isolated context per fetch. |
| `bypassCsp` |
`true` | Bypasses Content Security Policy via CDP `Page.setBypassCSP`, unlocking micro-frontend dyn

amic script loading. |
